hypothesis: Native Extract returns NotApplied on an empty pad because it resolves the source sample through a page/binding path that the layer borrow does not update
test: Decompile FUN_02903b90 and compare its source-sample walk with selection::current; write the provider into that exact path and retry
notes: FUN_02903b90 reads the layer sample at +0x4a8 and its holder at +0x4b0; the layer path was right, the null holder was the missing piece

hypothesis: Extract returns NotApplied because FUN_02903b90 requires the borrowed layer holder at +0x4b0, not just the sample at +0x4a8
test: Borrow both the provider sample and its +0x30 holder into the empty layer, then retry D04 synth
notes: Decompile shows holder check: a sample pointer with a null holder resolves to no source

hypothesis: Synth output quality depends on the selected sample because extract_take uses job.source.frames as the Extract end
test: Inspect extract_take and compare synth frame count on empty vs sampled pads
notes: The synth now uses rendered frames for end/source_frames; output length and content no longer inherit the source

hypothesis: Extract is the wrong workflow; Sample Select's native Load Sample path assigns a WAV to the selected pad
test: Trace Sample Select refs and decompile FUN_01a5bd00/FUN_01ecaf20/FUN_01ee0580/FUN_01a95ab0/FUN_01a95f90
notes: FUN_01a5bd00 takes a request (path at +0x38, pad at +0x40, layer at +0x44); FUN_01ecaf20 builds that request from a file

hypothesis: FUN_01a5bd00 request +0x38 is a sample key/path, not a C++ File object
test: Decompile FUN_02a2ed50 and verify it searches the pool by comparing +0x38 against sample+0xa8
notes: The request field is the pool lookup key; +0x40/+0x44 are pad/layer and -1 means load-only

hypothesis: The assignment helper crashed because Extract's live view/callback are command-owned; patching the Extract command's destination pad (+0x58) directly avoids a second command
test: Add destination to Extract Request/Arm, rewrite command+0x58 before execute, and verify the selected pad's sample changes
notes: Directly patching the Extract command destination +0x58 before execute writes the synth take onto the selected empty or populated pad; D04/D10/D11 emulator tests passed

hypothesis: Zero populated pads can be supported by a synthetic sample object with only zeroed metadata
test: Call FUN_02a43b40 with zero source fields, set frames/rate, and run Extract
notes: Extract needs a real provider object at sample+0x130+0x10; zeroed metadata is not enough

hypothesis: FUN_01ef4ac0 is the raw float32 sample constructor needed for zero-pad synth
test: Call FUN_01ef4ac0 with the synth buffer and inspect the returned sample geometry
notes: It returned a sample pair; registration through FUN_01a95c10/FUN_01a967d0 removed the missing-file modal

hypothesis: A sample created by FUN_01ef4ac0 can be assigned by writing its pair into the pad layer
test: Create the sample, write sample+holder into the destination layer, and open the pad
notes: App showed 'Sample not found / Sample 002.wav'; pool registration is required

hypothesis: Registering the raw sample through the record-complete command is sufficient for the app to accept it
test: Run FUN_01ef4ac0, then FUN_01a95c10/FUN_01a967d0, then write the pair to the pad
notes: Missing-file modal disappeared and the pad showed the sample

hypothesis: The registered raw sample has the synth's stereo geometry and audio
test: Read metadata and buffer after registration
notes: Observed channels=1, frames=80000, constant/DC waveform; FUN_01ef4ac0 input layout is not yet correct

hypothesis: The lab's synthetic pad event supplies a usable input object for record UI
test: Read input::held_input/last_press_obj during forced record fallback
notes: Both were 0x0, so send_note_on was not called with null input

hypothesis: The sample pool pointer is a stable field of g_surface
test: Scan g_surface for the live pool pointer captured at the record ctor
notes: Found at g_surface+0x1fc8

hypothesis: The memory reader addresses audio by frame in an interleaved float buffer
test: Decompile the raw builder memory-reader vtable read method and inspect its sample address calculation
notes: FUN_021ceab0 returns buffer + channels * frame_offset * 4; builder FUN_01ef4ac0 sets channels and frames = float_count / channels. This establishes addressing, not the cause of the previous mono/DC result.

hypothesis: The raw builder uses a hidden AArch64 result pointer rather than a normal first argument
test: Disassemble FUN_01ef4ac0 entry and trace its argument registers
notes: Entry saves x8 as result pointer; x0 is context, x1 vector, w2 channels and w3 sample rate. This does not establish how the previous experiment invoked it.

hypothesis: A project with no sample-pool entries or layer sample references reproduces the zero-pad failure
test: Load a project with its samples lists emptied and layer sample names and paths cleared; run the synth on A01
notes: mod/tests/emulator_synth_empty.py reported Synth: no sample to seed Extract on the loaded fixture. The test also checks assignment, stereo geometry and non-DC audio after a successful render; those checks remain unexercised until the fix exists.

hypothesis: The recording engine passes the app-owned Temporary Samples service as the raw builder context
test: Trace the builder caller and recording engine constructor through their arguments
notes: Static chain FUN_0149d710 -> FUN_019dcc50 -> FUN_01f17c90 stores argument 8 at engine+0xab0; FUN_01f176f0 -> FUN_01ef5120 -> FUN_01ef4ac0 forwards it. Live capture and lifetime remain to be verified.

hypothesis: Hooking FUN_01ef3330 during app startup captures the live Temporary Samples service used by recording
test: Install a temporary constructor hook and compare its captured object with record engine+0xab0 in the same boot
notes: Temporary hooks on FUN_01ef3330 and FUN_01f17c90 captured the same nonzero service pointer in one emulator boot; no heap address is used as a constant. Cross-boot and lifetime behavior remain unverified.

hypothesis: Passing interleaved stereo floats and the captured Temporary Samples service to FUN_01ef4ac0 produces a sample with the same geometry and waveform
test: Run a temporary in-process probe using the x8 return convention and inspect the sample metadata and memory buffer
notes: On an empty-project emulator, the x8 ABI and captured live context returned channels=2, frames=4096, rate=44100; the first interleaved pairs match the supplied ramp and opposite polarity, quantized to approximately 16-bit. Registration and assignment were not part of this test.

hypothesis: A correctly constructed stereo sample can be registered with the native record-complete command and used as an Extract provider
test: Register the known-ramp sample in the current pool, temporarily borrow it in the selected empty layer, and run Extract; inspect the resulting pad and audio
notes: In the zero-pad emulator, registered 4096-frame ramp used as temporary layer provider; Extract reported Synth: copy created and the selected pad contained 2 channels, 33075 frames, 44100 Hz, RMS 0.092. Modal, pitch, persistence and seed cleanup remain to check.

hypothesis: Extract can use a real but unregistered native sample as its temporary provider while registering its own output
test: Repeat the zero-pad render with the raw native seed but omit record-complete registration; verify the selected output, modal, and audio
notes: Fresh zero-sample fixture: no record-complete registration; Extract returned Synth: copy created, selected sample stereo 33075 frames at 44100 Hz, RMS 0.092; screenshot showed Bass C2 and no modal. After stopping the app, the saved project contained exactly one pool entry, Bass C2.wav; reload and reference cleanup need separate checks.

hypothesis: A silent native seed can be released after Extract replaces the borrowed layer without changing the output
test: Replace the test ramp with silence, hold the shared sample pair until Extract finishes, release it through the firmware shared-pointer helper, and verify the zero-pad audio and saved pool
notes: The short test passed, but a longer all-pads scan found the app restarted (NRestarts increased); the saved project was empty. Release cannot be considered safe. A retention comparison is needed to isolate the cause.

hypothesis: The Extract-created sample persists and retains the synth pitch after the app restarts
test: Stop and restart the app after the zero-pad render, inspect the saved pool and the reloaded selected sample, and measure its C2 fundamental
notes: After clearing the extra seed reference, the saved project contained one Bass C2.wav entry and one populated layer; after restart A01 displayed the waveform. Decoded stereo audio has 33075 frames and a 69 Hz peak, within 5 Hz of C2.

hypothesis: The borrowed seed can remain on a different source pad after Extract assigns the destination, corrupting the project
test: After a zero-pad render inspect every pad layer for the seed and compare the selected state with destination state
notes: After rendering into A01 from zero pads, the retained native seed remained at A02 with 4096 frames while A01 held the 33075-frame output; restoring the original borrowed slot alone did not remove that second reference.

hypothesis: Keeping one unregistered native seed alive for the process lifetime avoids the delayed restart after Extract
test: Retain the native seed instead of releasing it, rerun zero-pad rendering, scan all pads, and observe the same process and restart counter over time
notes: Retained seed, cleared extra layer reference, no restart during render and subsequent scan (NRestarts=0), and successful save/reload. Longer-term use, cancellation, and repeated renders need verification.

hypothesis: Clearing every extra layer reference to the native seed after Extract will leave only the requested pad and a valid saved project
test: Remove only pad-layer slots still pointing to the retained seed after successful Extract; scan all 128 pads, save and reload the project, and check for a firmware restart
notes: On one empty-project render, clearing only slots referencing the retained seed left A01 as the sole populated pad. NRestarts=0; saved pool and layers contain only Bass C2.wav; A01 displayed it after restart. Native cleanup and other scenarios need further verification.

hypothesis: The native sample-selection control clears the extra seed layer and updates ownership correctly
test: Replace direct zero writes with control operation 0x40d and value 0 for the seed pad; verify all pads, restart counter, saved project and reload
notes: Control 0x40d value 0 cleared the seed pad; a full scan found only A01, NRestarts=0, and the saved project contained one Bass C2.wav entry and one layer. The reloaded waveform and other scenarios remain to check.

hypothesis: The zero-pad path targets a non-default pad and the native cleanup never populates an extra pad
test: Run the same empty-project render with a different selected pad, scan all pads and inspect the saved project
notes: Empty project, select A05: 128-pad scan found only pad 5 populated, stereo 33075 frames at 44100 Hz, RMS 0.092; no process restart.

hypothesis: After a zero-pad render, rendering to another empty pad preserves the first sample and uses the existing provider path
test: In the same session render on pad 9 after creating pad 5, then check both pads, audio and restart counter
notes: After A05, rendering to A09 produced A05 and A09 but also left an unexpected provider copy on A01; a full pad scan revealed it.

hypothesis: Tracking pads that were empty before borrowing allows safe removal of only new provider copies
test: Snapshot occupancy before borrowing, use the native sample-selection setter only on newly populated provider copies excluding the destination, and repeat A05 then A09 with a full pad scan
notes: Fresh empty project: rendered A05 then A09 in the same process; full scans returned [4] then [4,8], with stereo 33075-frame output and NRestarts=0. Saved project contained exactly the two expected pool entries and layers 4 and 8. Existing sample audio comparison and cancellation remain.

hypothesis: Overwriting a populated destination preserves another existing pad and its sample audio
test: After reload with A05 and A09 populated, render onto A05, compare A09 waveform bytes and scan all pad slots
notes: A05 overwritten with A05 and A09 prepopulated produced an unexpected additional A01 provider copy, although A09 WAV SHA-256 remained unchanged. The occupied-source path did not snapshot or clean up provider copies.

hypothesis: Applying the same pre-render occupancy snapshot to a populated source prevents unwanted copies on overwrite
test: Record the current source sample and empty pads before rendering A05; check all pads and A09 waveform after overwrite
notes: After reloading the two-pad project, overwriting A05 left only pads A05 and A09 populated, produced stereo 33075-frame audio, preserved A09 WAV SHA-256 and reported NRestarts=0.

hypothesis: Leaving the Sample page while a zero-pad synth job is running cancels it without leaving the seed on a pad
test: Start a synth from a zero-sample project and immediately switch to SEQ, then inspect job status, all pad layers and restart counter
notes: Immediate DATA and SEQ events resulted in Synth: copy created and only A05 populated, with no restart. The render finished before a cancellation was observed, so this did not exercise the cancellation path.

hypothesis: Borrowing a populated provider for another pad preserves its decoded audio
test: Render onto empty A09 using the A05 Bass C2 provider and compare the provider WAV samples before and after within stock re-encoding tolerance
notes: A05 to empty A09 yielded exactly pads A05/A09; the provider WAV contained 66150 float32 values and the before/after maximum difference was 0.0.

hypothesis: The durable empty-project regression reproduces the successful A05 path with the expected synth pitch
test: Generate a zero-sample project using make_empty_project.py, load it into the emulator, and run emulator_synth_empty.py --pad 5
notes: Passed: only A05 populated, stereo 33075 frames at 44100 Hz, RMS 0.09215, 69 Hz peak, no app modal or restart. The first run checked the screen before the menu repainted and produced a false modal detection; waiting for repaint resolved it.

hypothesis: When the synth worker is still running, leaving Sample Mode cancels and removes the temporary provider without assigning a pad
test: Use a temporary three-second render delay, send DATA then SEQ immediately, wait for completion, and scan all pads and restart counter
notes: With a three-second test delay, DATA followed by SEQ still rendered successfully on A05, with no restart. The menu consumes non-encoder buttons while open, so SEQ did not leave Sample Mode; cancellation was not reached.

hypothesis: The cancellation cleanup restores all zero-pad layers when finalize detects a different page
test: Temporarily force the finalize cancellation branch for synth, run from an empty project, and inspect all pad slots, status, saved project and restart count
notes: A temporary forced cancellation in finalize yielded Synth: cancelled, no occupied pads in the 128-pad scan, unchanged PID and NRestarts=0. After stop, the saved project had zero pool entries and no sample layers. This tests the branch, not a physical page-change trigger.

hypothesis: Installing the sample-service hook through the SDK site table preserves the zero-pad synth behavior
test: Build minimod against the modified SDK checkout, load a zero-sample project, and run the full empty-pad emulator regression
notes: SDK site-table hook and SDK silent_seed API passed the A05 empty-project regression: stereo 33075 frames at 44100 Hz, 69 Hz peak, no modal or restart, only A05 populated.

hypothesis: The published SDK tag works as minimod’s remote dependency for zero-pad synth rendering
test: Build minimod against remote SDK v0.1.9 and run the A05 empty-project emulator regression
notes: Cargo resolved v0.1.9 to 185c41c6; the packaged build and regression passed with only A05 populated, 33075 stereo frames at 44100 Hz, 69 Hz peak and no restart.

hypothesis: The rendered sample is silent because Extract assigns it to an inactive pad layer on empty pads
test: Compare the serialized layer active flag and capture emulator PCM while triggering the rendered pad versus a working pad; then activate the layer through the app's own parameter path and retest
notes: On a valid fresh synth project, A01 PCM was all zero with active=false. Changing only the saved layer active flag to true, reloading, and pressing A01 produced PCM RMS 306.485, peak 3868, with 65,056 nonzero samples. Extract-created WAV was valid (stereo 33075 frames, RMS 0.09215, 69 Hz).

hypothesis: Control 0x44e activates an Extract-assigned synth layer whose serialized active flag is false
test: After one synth render, issue only control 0x44e with value 1; inspect the serialized active flag and pad PCM versus the working pad
notes: The empty-project harness rendered a valid Bass C2 on A01, but saved active remained false. 0x44e did not enable playback; it has been removed from the implementation.

hypothesis: Control 0x45c enables an Extract-assigned synth layer for pad playback
test: After one fresh empty-project render issue only control 0x45c with value 1; save, reload, verify active=true and capture nonzero PCM
notes: Fresh empty-project harness rendered valid stereo audio (RMS 0.09215, 69 Hz) but saved active remained false. 0x45c did not enable the layer.

hypothesis: The serialized active byte is at the first layer element reached through padState+0x1d08, then +0x28
test: After a fresh empty-project render set only *(padState+0x1d08)+0x28 to 1; save and reload, verify active=true and capture the pad PCM
notes: Fresh empty-project render succeeded, but the layer still saved active=false. The surface pad slot vector is not the serializer input.

hypothesis: The serializer layer vector belongs to the program object at pageState+0x2310, so its first layer active byte is program+0x1d08+0x28
test: After a fresh empty-project render set only the program object layer byte to 1; save/reload, verify active=true and capture nonzero PCM
notes: Write/readback succeeded (probe 8), but PAD 1 PCM remained all zeros and save/reload still reported active=false. This serializer-model vector is not the live playback activation.

hypothesis: The native 0x44e activation route requires selector 0x101 for A01 rather than the zero-based pad index
test: After one fresh empty-project render call control 0x44e with selector 0x101 and value 1; inspect saved active and capture PAD 1 PCM
notes: Rendered sample was valid, but after the 0x44e call A01 PCM stayed all zeros and saved active remained false.

hypothesis: Control 0x45c with selector 0x101 activates the A01 playback layer
test: After one fresh empty-project render call only control 0x45c with selector 0x101 and value 1; save/reload and capture A01 PCM
notes: After a fresh render, A01 PCM remained all zeros and the project still saved active=false.

hypothesis: The runtime sample-layer object at padState+0x22e8 has its audio enable flag at +0x28
test: After an empty-project synth render set only layerContext+0x28 to 1; capture PAD 1 PCM immediately before save
notes: The write was applied on a fresh synth render, but A01 PCM remained all zero. This runtime object is not the audio activation field.

hypothesis: The Extract runtime path can set the layer active through a verified firmware-owned operation
test: Apply the operation that changes the saved layer active flag in memory after Extract, then verify live PCM and save/reload persistence
notes: The SDK pads::set_layer_active API writes the Ghidra-confirmed InstrumentLayer::active byte after Extract. Fresh render produced nonzero PCM immediately; save/reload preserved active=true and nonzero PCM.

hypothesis: The firmware’s pad-layer UI action identifies a callable operation that activates the selected layer and updates the audio graph
test: Use GhidraMCP to decompile the known layer-control handlers and their nearby callers; identify the exact setter/action, then invoke only that operation after a synth Extract and check saved active plus PCM
notes: The candidate UI handlers and control operations were unrelated/ineffective. Ghidra identified InstrumentLayer::active at +0xb18; setting that field through the SDK API after Extract directly updated live playback and persisted, so no separate UI action is needed.

hypothesis: The pad control operation immediately after sample assignment (0x40e) enables the layer
test: Use GhidraMCP FindConst to identify call sites and the setter dispatch for 0x40e; confirm whether the operation targets layer active before trying it once after Extract
notes: GhidraMCP scan found the same controller table places 0x40e next to the kLayer1RootNote mapping (0x40d is kLayer1Sample); it is a note property, not the layer active toggle.

hypothesis: The pad control operation immediately before kLayer1Sample (0x40c) toggles layer active
test: Use GhidraMCP FindConst to identify 0x40c call sites and inspect the associated key/field; if it maps to active, invoke it once on a fresh synth output and verify live PCM and persistence
notes: GhidraMCP call-site mapping ties the 0x40c block to the firmware’s kKeygroupKeytrack property, not the serialized sample-layer active field.

hypothesis: The Extract assignment command exposes a native post-assignment step that activates the destination layer
test: Use GhidraMCP to decompile the already identified assignment constructor and execute path; confirm whether it writes or notifies the serialized active property, then reuse or extend that native command path
notes: GhidraMCP decompilation of FUN_01a9a290 shows only native setter ops 0x40d (sample assignment) and 0x45e (velocity selection); no active change or layer activation notification.

hypothesis: The destination pad’s InstrumentLayer object has its live active byte at +0xb18, and setting it after Extract enables playback
test: On one fresh zero-pad render, set only *(destinationPadState+0x22e8)+0xb18 to 1 after native Extract; capture immediate pad PCM and inspect the saved active flag
notes: GhidraMCP decompilation of the InstrumentLayer vtable (FUN_029159a0) shows Active serialized from +0xb18. The v0.1.10 SDK helper set this byte after a fresh A01 Extract; live state readback was 1, PCM while held RMS 495.95/peak 3868/42,596 nonzero samples, and saved/reloaded project remained active=true with PCM RMS 495.99/peak 3868/43,090 nonzero samples.

hypothesis: The SDK active-layer API addresses a non-default destination pad correctly
test: Render into A05 on a fresh empty project using remote SDK v0.1.10; confirm only A05 is populated, its live active byte is 1, and pressing it yields nonzero PCM
notes: Remote SDK v0.1.10 render on A05 populated only pad index 4; its InstrumentLayer active byte read 1 and pressing A05 yielded PCM RMS 1634.62, peak 12717, 43,202 nonzero samples.

hypothesis: The seed workflow writes the holder at layer + 0x958 instead of the native holder field at layer + 0x4b0
test: Compare the pointer calculation against the documented and SDK-confirmed layer layout
notes: Seed sample slot is layer+0x4a8; adding 0x4b0 targets layer+0x958. Firmware decompilation command-execution.txt reads the companion at layer+0x4b0. Runtime impact remains to be tested.

hypothesis: Extract command execution is synchronous with the Sample-page handler on the same thread
test: Log thread ID and entry/exit order around the native handler and Extract execute hook during one emulator render
notes: Emulator synth trace: handler enter, execute enter, execute exit, handler exit all on tid 9343; Ghidra handler -> command manager -> vtable +0x40 -> Extract execute agrees. Other command paths not tested.
